name: Schizachyrium

project_scope.note: The current project pool has one canonical Schizachyrium anchor; species taxonomy/range decisions remain in the species package.

recognition.where_to_look_first: Native little bluestem shows DISTINCT relatively tight bunches and many SHORT silvery racemes terminating separate leafy upper branches. Introduced KR bluestem instead presents several LONG fingerlike racemes gathered into one terminal panicle; both require same-plant leaf collars and paired spikelet macro.
priority: numerous separate SHORT terminal or axillary racemes throughout upper culm
true leaf collar and mature paired spikelets
short terminal fuzzy racemes on branchlets

comparisons.rule: Schizachyrium scatters many short racemes across branched upper stems; Bothriochloa concentrates its rames into a more unified terminal head whose node hair and branch architecture are major ID clues.
Anatherum glomeratum builds a dense brushlike fluffy crown; Schizachyrium scoparium shows repeated short racemes terminating separate upper branchlets.

cross_genus_bluestem_comparison.title: KR BLUESTEM vs LITTLE BLUESTEM — our Central Texas native/invasive decision
cross_genus_bluestem_comparison.memory_rule: A FEW LONG fingers together (KR) versus MANY SHORT fuzzy racemes on SEPARATE upper branches (little bluestem).
quick_split: KR / Bothriochloa ischaemum — introduced Old World bluestem; terminal panicle typically 3–8 or more elongated fingerlike spikelet-bearing branches. Leaf UPPER surface just above collar may have stiff papilla-based hairs. Node hair sources conflict; not a single-character proof.

Little bluestem / Schizachyrium scoparium — Hays native, generally dense persistent bunch; many short racemes arise from different branches in the upper plant and become silvery/fluffy in fruit. Roots/leaf collar and actual spikelet pairs strengthen ID.
field_crew_sequence: Photograph rooted whole clump and top-to-bottom reproductive architecture.
Trace WHERE each raceme originates: all near one terminal center = KR candidate; dispersed short units on many upper culm branches = little bluestem candidate.
At 10×, inspect KR upper leaf surface right above collar for papilla-based hairs; check true ligule on same culm.
Check paired sessile fertile/pedicelled companion spikelet details with 1-mm scale; where unresolved label bluestem sp.
Before removal or seed collection, rule out native cane bluestem and silver bluestem plus introduced Kleberg bluestem.
cross_genus_bluestem_comparison.node_hair_caution: Do not enforce smooth KR nodes: Texas A&M calls songarica nodes hairless; local UT Austin morphological work reports short or appressed hairs. Use combined characters. Cane bluestem tends to bear a pronounced BEARD at nodes.

cross_genus_bluestem_comparison.first_clue: KR bluestem (introduced): look for several long, slender fingerlike flowering branches clustered together at the tip of a stem. Native little bluestem has shorter fuzzy flowering branches along separate upper stems.

expert_collar_and_node_notes.Leaf collar: On a confirmed same-plant specimen, inspect stiff papilla-based hairs on the upper leaf blade near the collar; photograph the true ligule with a ruler.
expert_collar_and_node_notes.Spikelet pairs: At 10–20× magnification, separate an attached sessile fertile spikelet from its pedicelled companion and check the awn; the current photos do not resolve this.
expert_collar_and_node_notes.Node-hair caution: Do NOT use hairless stem nodes as a required test. Texas A&M describes glabrous KR nodes, while local UT Austin treatments have noted short hairs. A heavy beard is useful when considering native cane bluestem.
expert_collar_and_node_notes.Native versus invasive decision: Use multiple characters and preserve the project's nonnative invasive-comparison status; never remove native bluestem on a seedhead silhouette alone.

items.label: B. ischaemum species habit — non-Texas example
items.image_role: Whole plant in flower — European species-level habit reference, not a confirmed Texas var. songarica specimen
items.caption: Full rooted-looking tuft with flowering culms and several terminal heads from Austria. This is the accepted species B. ischaemum, but NOT a Texas-vouchered King Ranch / songarica plant. It teaches overall habit only; do not use its crown form as a diagnostic Texas-variety character.
items.why_it_matters: The page previously opened on a detached seedhead without any whole-plant context. This wider view makes it easier to recognize the growth form while documenting regional limits.

items.label: KR bluestem — straw-colored flowering racemes
